Field records from the Ivory Coast and Gabon suggest that these mass values are remarkably consistent across the species' geographic range.

In comparison, smaller duiker species such as the blue duiker (Philantomba monticola) rarely exceed 12 years in captivity, suggesting that the Bay duiker's larger body mass confers a survival advantage. The protracted intrauterine development also permits the foetus to attain the relatively large neonatal mass that characterizes this species.
